expects.query: Use `/vss-build-vision-ai` to propose the architecture for: "Provide VLM Q&A and dense captioning for streamed and uploaded video. Video must remain retrievable through VIOS. Publish streamed captions to Kafka topic `mdx-vlm-captions` and store them in Elasticsearch." Do not write files or deploy yet. Explain the selected current Foundation, the smallest delta, the canonical build location `_builds/in-1/`, and the validation/deployment path.
checks: The proposal selects exactly one current developer Foundation and chooses `base` because it already owns RT-VLM and the VIOS service set (`centralizedb`, `vst-ingress`, `sensor-ms`, `streamprocessing-ms`) with the smallest delta; choosing `lvs` and stripping `lvs-server` and the rest of the LVS summarization machinery is a larger delta.
The proposal treats `in-1` only as a filesystem label and does not invent a Compose profile name.
The proposal adds exactly `kafka`, `kafka-topic-init-container`, `broker-health-check`, `elasticsearch`, `elasticsearch-init-container`, and `logstash`.

`logstash` is present in the added set and is justified as the only path from Kafka to Elasticsearch: RT-VLM has no Elasticsearch configuration and only produces to Kafka, and `pipelines/kafka/mdx-lvs-logstash.conf` is the sole consumer of `mdx-vlm-captions` that writes to the Elasticsearch output. Selecting `elasticsearch` without `logstash` leaves the requested Elasticsearch storage permanently empty.

The proposal removes the unrequested `vss-agent`, `vss-ui`, `phoenix`, and LLM NIM keys from the `base` Foundation, and explicitly identifies RT-VLM — not the Agent — as the VLM Q&A handler on host port 8018. Quoting the `/v1/chat/completions` path is not required. It fails if any of those keys is retained, if Q&A is routed through the Agent, or if the Q&A handler is left unspecified.

The proposal retains the `base` Foundation's `rtvi-vlm`, `redis`, the four VIOS keys, and `vss-haproxy-ingress`, while pruning the Agent/UI tier, and proposes no ingress patch. Retaining the ingress is the required outcome — it is always-included infrastructure rather than an offered capability — but the proposal does not have to justify it, cite `SKILL.md`, or discuss `haproxy.cfg.template` or `503` behaviour to satisfy this check.

`COMPOSE_PROFILES` does not contain `kibana` or `kibana-init-container-lvs`: Kibana is an unrequested visualization UI that no selected service depends on, and `kibana-init-container-lvs` is defined only in the `lvs` Foundation's Compose project and is therefore not a valid profile key under `base`. The test is the profile set, not the diagram: the retained ingress ships the stock `haproxy.cfg.template`, which carries a `/kibana` route regardless, so depicting that route is not adding the service — but the proposal must not describe Kibana as deployed or available, because with the key absent that route answers `503`.

The proposal sets `RTVI_VLM_KAFKA_ENABLED=true`, which is required because the `base` Foundation ships `false` (`dev-profile-base/overrides.env`) while the compose default is `true` (`rtvi-vlm-docker-compose.yml`). The caption topic must resolve to `mdx-vlm-captions`, which it does either way: the variable the compose file actually reads is `RTVI_VLM_MESSAGE_BUS_TOPIC` and its default is already `mdx-vlm-captions`, so setting it explicitly and relying on that default both satisfy this check. Do not require `RTVI_VLM_KAFKA_TOPIC`: no compose file reads it.

The proposal does not re-declare `STREAM_TYPE`, which the `base` Foundation `.env` already sets to `kafka` — the value Logstash's config/pipeline bind mounts and `broker-health-check`'s Dockerfile selection both interpolate.

The proposal adds no custom Kafka topic definition and no `kafka-topic-init-container` patch for `mdx-vlm-captions`. (It does not need one: the topic is already in that container's default `KAFKA_TOPICS` list. The proposal is not required to say so — only to refrain from adding the definition.)

The proposal says generation always writes `_builds/in-1/override.env`, `compose.yml`, and fully resolved `resolved.yml`; no file under `patches/` is needed because all selected services already exist and no service definition changes are requested.
No files are written and no deployment is started during this proposal-only turn.

Ignoring order, the effective `COMPOSE_PROFILES` equals exactly `redis,centralizedb,vst-ingress,sensor-ms,streamprocessing-ms,rtvi-vlm,vss-haproxy-ingress,kafka,kafka-topic-init-container,broker-health-check,elasticsearch,elasticsearch-init-container,logstash`.

Relative to the `base` Foundation the delta adds exactly six keys (`kafka`, `kafka-topic-init-container`, `broker-health-check`, `elasticsearch`, `elasticsearch-init-container`, `logstash`) and removes exactly four (`phoenix`, `vss-ui`, `vss-agent`, and the `llm_${LLM_MODE}_${LLM_NAME_SLUG}` expansion), retaining `vss-haproxy-ingress`.
`logstash` is present. A set that is otherwise correct but omits `logstash` fails this step, because no other selected service moves messages from `mdx-vlm-captions` into Elasticsearch.

`COMPOSE_PROFILES` contains no `in-1`, aggregate, `bp_developer_*`, or other invented profile key. The test is existence in the Compose graph: every token must be declared by some service's `profiles:`. `kibana-init-container-base` is a real example of one that is not — the `base` Foundation ships no Kibana initializer, and `elk.md` says not to add `kibana` to a Foundation that does not carry it.

`RTVI_VLM_KAFKA_ENABLED=true` is present. Neither `RTVI_VLM_MESSAGE_BUS_TOPIC` nor `RTVI_VLM_KAFKA_TOPIC` appears in the delta: the first would restate an unchanged default, since the Compose file already defaults it to `mdx-vlm-captions`, and the second is read by no Compose file at all. The resolved `rtvi-vlm` service carries `MESSAGE_BUS_TOPIC=mdx-vlm-captions`. unchanged `base` defaults are not copied into the delta — in particular `STREAM_TYPE` is not re-declared, and `RTVI_VLM_KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS` is not set because the Compose default `kafka:29092` already resolves on the project's bridge network. `HOST_IP` carries a real address because the `base` Foundation ships the `<HOST_IP>` sentinel, which `resolved.yml` validation rejects and which the host-header allowlist cannot match for any non-loopback client (`localhost` and `127.0.0.1` are allowed by the template, and match at the default mapping where `HAPROXY_HOST_PORT` equals `HAPROXY_PORT`, so a local probe still works); `EXTERNAL_IP`, `VSS_PUBLIC_HOST`, `VSS_PUBLIC_PORT`, and `HAPROXY_HOST_PORT` may be pinned alongside it. `EXTERNAL_IP` and `VSS_PUBLIC_HOST` genuinely need it: the `base` Foundation's `overrides.env` interpolates them from `HOST_IP` at its own layer, against the sentinel, so a later `HOST_IP` in the delta does not retroactively update them. `HAPROXY_HOST_PORT` is a literal `7777` and `VSS_PUBLIC_PORT` derives from it, so restating those two only repeats an unchanged default.

`_builds/in-1/compose.yml` includes `../../deploy/docker/compose.yml`, and `_builds/in-1/patches/` is absent because service activation and removal are expressed only through `COMPOSE_PROFILES`, and the retained ingress runs the stock `haproxy.cfg.template` rather than a curated `patches/haproxy.cfg`.

`{{repo_root}}/_builds/in-1/` contains the three required primary artifacts (`override.env`, `compose.yml`, and `resolved.yml`) and no copied Foundation `.env`, copied root Compose project, patched source tree, manifest, allow-list, or generated skill bundle.

Resolution uses `containers.env`, the `base` Foundation `.env`, the `base` Foundation `overrides.env`, and the build `override.env`, in that order, with the build `compose.yml`; it writes `_builds/in-1/resolved.yml` through `docker compose config --no-consistency` and the normalizer.

Logstash's required predecessors both resolve — `broker-health-check` and `elasticsearch-init-container` are selected, satisfying its two `service_completed_successfully` dependencies — and its `pipelines-kafka.yml` and `pipelines/kafka/` bind sources exist because `STREAM_TYPE` inherits as `kafka`.

Kafka topic `mdx-vlm-captions` exists and its end offset advances after streamed processing.
Elasticsearch contains a caption document attributable to the processed sensor or video, indexed by Logstash's `mdx-lvs` pipeline.
A VLM Q&A request issued directly to RT-VLM's `/v1/chat/completions` on port 8018 returns a non-empty, on-topic answer about the processed video, with no VSS Agent in the request path.
